summary.value: The Ardennaise is an old farm chicken of the Ardennes uplands, a region shared by southern Belgium and north-eastern France. It was first written up in 1882, did well under a Liege breeders' club from 1893, then declined as Italian laying hens flooded in and local birds were crossed with Leghorns. By 1940 the pure breed had gone, and breeders spent about thirty years after the war rebuilding it. It is related to the Bresse Gauloise and is bred in twelve colors, often with a dark face. A bantam form dates from the early 1900s, and a rumpless strain lacks a tail entirely. Hens weigh about 3.5 pounds and cocks about 4.5. Hens lay around 140 to 180 white eggs a year, medium in size. The birds are slender, lively and hardy, and are kept for both eggs and meat by conservation minded keepers.
